newsitem.title: JAPAN: US won't recognise new Cambodia co-premier - Solarz.
newsitem.headline: US won't recognise new Cambodia co-premier - Solarz.

text.p: The U.S. special envoy on Cambodia, Stephen Solarz, told Japan on Monday that Washington will not recognise Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot as a replacement for ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, Kyodo News Service reported.
Solarz made the comment in a meeting in Tokyo with Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda.
A U.S. embassy spokesman had no comment on the report.

The Cambodian National Assembly is expected to select Ung Huot as the country's co-leader on July 28. Solarz said the United States was concerned the decision would not be an expression of the assembly's free will because a number of its legislators would not be present.

The former U.S. congressman is visiting Japan on his way to Beijing to meet Cambodian head of state King Norodom Sihanouk. Solarz said he believed about 20 legislators loyal to Prince Ranariddh had gone into exile and could not attend the session.
Solarz is President Bill Clinton's special envoy on the Cambodian crisis, which erupted when the country's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen ousted the prince from power earlier this month.
